title: 1955 AHSME Problem 19
statement: Two numbers whose sum is \(6\) and the absolute value of whose difference is \(8\) are roots of the equation:

solutions.text:
Taking the larger number first, \[ u+v=6,\qquad u-v=8 \] gives \(u=7\) and \(v=-1.\) Their product is \(-7,\) so the monic equation with these roots is \[ x^2-6x-7=0. \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Solve \(u+v=6\) and \(u-v=8\) after choosing an order
A monic quadratic with roots \(u,v\) is \(x^2-(u+v)x+uv\)
